body:
cc @whatwg/canvas

Regarding `currentColor`, there was https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/9940 which seems related, though it apparently missed a few cases: https://jsfiddle.net/pau1bt6k/
 - Safari will honor the `<canvas>`'s current color, if it's set through the element's `style` attribute, but not if it's set through a stylesheet.
 - Firefox will honor the actual current color, but doesn't support `color-mix()` in there, and thus fails the tests.
 - Chrome will only honor the current color if it's set through the `style` attribute, *and* part of a `color-mix()` call. They pass the tests...

There is also the question of CSS custom properties (`var(--)`), which no browser support.

In canvas rendering, **context-dependent color values** are usually resolved at the moment the color is assigned to the drawing state (for example, via `fillStyle` or `strokeStyle`).

Examples of context-dependent values include:

* `currentColor` — resolves to the computed CSS `color` value of the associated canvas element.
* CSS custom properties (`var(--color)`) — are resolved using the element's computed styles before the final color is used.
* System colors and theme-dependent colors — are resolved according to the browser's current UI/theme settings.
* Relative color functions (`color-mix()`, `hsl(from ...)`, etc.) — are computed into an absolute color before drawing. ([[MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/color_value?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][1])

For a 2D canvas:

1. The browser parses the supplied color string as a CSS `<color>` value.
2. Any context-dependent references are resolved against the canvas element's current computed style and environment.
3. The resulting color is converted into the canvas context's color space (typically `srgb`, though `display-p3` can be requested). ([[TypeError](https://www.typeerror.org/docs/dom/canvasrenderingcontext2d/fillstyle?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][2])
4. The resolved color is stored in the canvas drawing state and used for subsequent drawing operations.

For example:

```js
canvas.style.color = "blue";
ctx.fillStyle = "currentColor";
ctx.fillRect(0, 0, 100, 100);
```

Here, `currentColor` resolves to `blue` based on the canvas element's computed `color` property before the rectangle is painted. ([[MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/color_value?utm_source=chatgpt.com)][1])

If you're referring to a specific framework or platform called "Canvas" (for example, Figma Canvas, Power Apps Canvas, or Flutter Canvas), I can explain how that environment resolves color values as well.

[1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/color_value?utm_source=chatgpt.com "<color> - CSS | MDN"
[2]: https://www.typeerror.org/docs/dom/canvasrenderingcontext2d/fillstyle?utm_source=chatgpt.com "CanvasRenderingContext2D.fillStyle - DOM Documentation - TypeError"

> ### Aký je problém so štandardom HTML?
> Keď sú farby (t. j. `fillStyle`, `strokeStyle`a `shadowColor`) nastavené na plátne, [špecifikácia](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) hovorí:
> 
> > Ak je na vykonanie rozlíšenia potrebná hodnota iných vlastností elementu a (napríklad rozlíšenie aktuálnej farby alebo systémovej farby), použite _element_ , ak bol odovzdaný, alebo počiatočné hodnoty vlastností, ak nie.
> 
> To znamená, že dĺžky relatívne k písmu (napr. `em`) by mali byť relatívne k `font`prvku (alebo k pôvodnému písmu v prípade OffscreenCanvas), ale to sa líši od toho, ako sa s nimi zaobchádza pri iných hodnotách (napr. `letterSpacing`), ktoré ich riešia relatívne k písmu plátna (toto nie je špecifikované a je o tom diskutované v [#10893](https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10893) , ale je konzistentné vo všetkých prehliadačoch).
> 
> Taktiež nešpecifikuje, ako by sa mali riešiť hodnoty závislé od kontextu iného ako vlastnosti elementu kontextu, ako napríklad relatívne dĺžky koreňového písma/výrezu (napr. `rem`alebo `vw`) alebo `light-dark()`.
> 
> Existujúce implementácie nie sú konzistentné v spôsobe, akým spracovávajú tieto hodnoty:
> 
> Hodnota	Chróm	Gekón	WebKit
> `rgb(calc(7px / 1px) 1 0)`	prijaté	zamietnutý	prijaté
> `rgb(calc(1em / 1px) 1 0)`	rieši sa, akoby `em`bolo`0px`	zamietnutý	zamietnutý
> `rgb(calc(1rem / 1px) 1 0)`	rieši sa, akoby `rem`bolo`0px`	zamietnutý	zamietnutý
> `rgb(calc(1vw / 1px) 1 0)`	rieši sa, akoby `vw`bolo`0px`	zamietnutý	zamietnutý
> `currentColor`	rozhoduje sa na #000000	rozhoduje sa o farbe elementu (čierna pre OffscreenCanvas)	rozhoduje sa na #000000
> `light-dark(red, green)`	zamietnutý	vždy sa rozpozná ako svetelná možnosť pre `<canvas>`, zamietnuté pre OffscreenCanvas	zamietnutý

### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

When colors (i.e. `fillStyle`, `strokeStyle` and `shadowColor`) are set on a canvas [the spec](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-color/#parse-a-css-color-value) says:

> "If the value of other properties on the element a <color> is on is required to do the resolution (such as resolving a currentcolor or system color), use _element_ if it was passed, or the initial values of the properties if not."

This implies font-relative lengths (e.g. `em`) should be relative to the `font` of the element (or the initial font in the case of OffscreenCanvas) but this differs from how they are handled on other values (e.g. `letterSpacing`) which resolve them relative to the canvas' font (this is unspecified and in discussion in #10893 but consistent across browsers).

It also doesn't specify how values dependent on context other than the properties of the context element, such as root-font/viewport relative lengths (e.g. `rem` or `vw`) or `light-dark()`, should be resolved.

Existing implementations aren't consistent in how they handle these values:

| Value | Chromium | Gecko | WebKit |
|-|---|---|---|
| `rgb(calc(7px / 1px) 1 0)` | accepted | rejected | accepted |
| `rgb(calc(1em / 1px) 1 0)` | resolves as though `em` was `0px` | rejected | rejected |
| `rgb(calc(1rem / 1px) 1 0)` | resolves as though `rem` was `0px` | rejected | rejected |
| `rgb(calc(1vw / 1px) 1 0)` | resolves as though `vw` was `0px` | rejected | rejected |
| `currentColor` | resolves to #000000 | resolves to element color (black for OffscreenCanvas)  | resolves to #000000 |
| `light-dark(red, green)` | rejected | always resolves to light option for `<canvas>`, rejected for OffscreenCanvas | rejected |

> There is also the question of CSS custom properties (var(--)), which no browser support.

I think, as written currently, [the spec](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#arbitrary-substitution-function) is pretty clear that `var()` (and any other arbitrary substitution function) is invalid here, whether that is the desired behavior is another question: 

> Unless otherwise specified, arbitrary substitution functions can be used in place of any part of any property’s value (including within other functional notations); and are not valid in any other context.

Note that there is language in the spec for filter assignments containing context dependent values, see https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#filters

"When the value of the [current filter](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#concept-canvas-current-filter) is a string parsable as a [<filter-value-list>](https://drafts.csswg.org/filter-effects/#typedef-filter-value-list) which defines lengths using percentages or using ['em'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#em) or ['ex'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values/#ex) units, these must be interpreted relative to the [computed value](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) of the ['font-size'](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-fonts/#font-size-prop) property of the [font style source object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#font-style-source-object) at the time that the attribute is set. If the [computed values](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-cascade/#computed-value) are undefined for a particular case (e.g. because the [font style source object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#font-style-source-object) is not an element or is not [being rendered](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/rendering.html#being-rendered)), then the relative keywords must be interpreted relative to the default value of the [font](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/canvas.html#dom-context-2d-font) attribute. The 'larger' and 'smaller' keywords are not supported."

The "not being rendered" part covers OffscreenCanvas.

Is the spec missing a similar statement for computationally dependent color-related values in an OffscreenCanvas (similar to the wording for filter)?

Note that there are some WPT's for context dependent values in OffscreenCanvas here: https://wpt.fyi/results/html/canvas/offscreen/fill-and-stroke-styles?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=2d.fillStyle.parse.invalid

I have a fix for the failing cases in Blink that should land soon: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/chromium/src/+/8508299

There are some significant privacy issues here to account for:
* currentColor may be a visited link color if the canvas is inside a link element
* System colors can reveal accessibility settings via the active UA theme, not to mention AccentColor.

If the spec clears this up it needs language about tainting, though tainting would be harder to implement than refusing to allow the use of these colors or substituting generic values. We learned a lot about these challenges while implementing HTML-in-Canvas.

> There are some significant privacy issues here to account for:
> 
>     * currentColor may be a visited link color if the canvas is inside a link element
> 
>     * System colors can reveal accessibility settings via the active UA theme, not to mention AccentColor.

Aren't these resolving to the same values `getComputedStyle(canvas)` would resolve to?

> 11\. > There are some significant privacy issues here to account for:
>      > ```
>      > * currentColor may be a visited link color if the canvas is inside a link element
>      > 
>      > * System colors can reveal accessibility settings via the active UA theme, not to mention AccentColor.
>      > ```
>      
>      
>      Aren't these resolving to the same values `getComputedStyle(canvas)` would resolve to?

Yes, implementations can be sure to use the same mechanisms as `getComputedStyle`. The spec would need to be explicit about this, as there are multiple paths to getting the currentColor, or any color, and the implementation must use the correct one.

The technical point, I suppose, is that it's much easier to implement "never use the visited color" than it is to implement "use the visited dependent color but taint the canvas if the link is visited".

Tainting the canvas only if the link has been visited would leak the fact the link has been visited, so that wouldn't be great 😄.
My point is more that, API wise, this would not surface any new privacy vector. The CSS specs could certainly do with a more robust specification in that area, since, unless I missed it, it's not really specified how `:visited` should be ignored even by `getComputedStyle`; but I suppose it's fair for the HTML side to assume this is handled there.

Just to clarify here, the privacy issues mentioned shouldn't apply to OffscreenCanvas since it doesn't exist in the DOM. This means there's no possibility of it being inside of a link element or getting a non-default currentColor. 

These issues may exist for regular DOM-connected canvas elements and the spec may still need updating for both cases.
